title: Verifier Halting Verdict
statement: Let $S$ and $V$ be finite deterministic Turing machines over the binary alphabet, let $x,y$ be binary inputs, and let $c$ be a configuration of $V$ on $y$ whose state is halted. Choose any Boolean boundary tag, any input-head position for $x$, any contents for the work tapes of $S$, any work-head positions for $S$, and any bit $b$. One step of the host machine from the corresponding verifier-phase configuration halts and has output the one-bit word whose bit is true exactly when $c$'s output is the one-bit word $[1]$.
hypotheses_covered: A configuration $c$ of $V$ on $y$ with halted state
Arbitrary contents of the scheduler work tapes
replaced: Let $S, V$ be deterministic machines and $d$ a halted verifier configuration. For any choice bit, one host step from the verifier-phase configuration for $d$ halts the host and emits the single bit recording whether the complete output of $d$ is exactly the one-bit string $1$.
